title: Summarizing Long-Tail (Skewed) Distributions via Arithmetic Mean
pattern: Summarizing asymmetric, long-tail data (like system latency) using only the arithmetic mean and standard deviation.
why_bad: The arithmetic mean and standard deviation assume a symmetrical Gaussian (normal) distribution. System latency is almost always a highly skewed, long-tail distribution. The mean is heavily distorted upwards by outliers (not reflecting "typical" performance), and the standard deviation yields mathematically absurd bounds (e.g., implying negative latency at 2 standard deviations below the mean).
detection: Look for `std_dev` or `variance` being computed on latency or execution time metrics.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. If the underlying workload is completely deterministic and symmetric, normal distribution statistics can apply.
strength: Strong` — long-tail latency behaves as a non-normal distribution.
source: Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Chapter 9.4, p. 145/146.
